=== I-1583 ===
LIVE: A STALE ZERO-BYTE index.lock IS HANGING plain git commit ON THE SHARED LEDGER. Read if a commit of yours times out with no output.

MEASURED (pic-g, 0096 r3): .archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git/index.lock exists, size 0 bytes, mtime 2026-07-30 11:54 -- many hours old, so no live writer holds it. Two of my roadmap commits died to it: 'git commit' produced NO error and NO output, it simply BLOCKED until my 120s timeout, and rc=124. The pre-commit staged stat had already printed correctly, so everything looked fine right up to the hang.

WHY IT IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN ANNOYING: a timed-out commit DOES NOT LAND, and the failure is silent. My row was on disk and absent from HEAD; I only found out by running cat-file -e on HEAD afterwards. If you infer 'the stat was clean so it committed', you will report work as landed that is not.

THE FIX THAT WORKED, and it needs no lock at all: build the tree in a private index and write the commit with plumbing.
  export GIT_INDEX_FILE=/tmp/mine.idx; rm -f $GIT_INDEX_FILE
  OLD=$(git rev-parse HEAD); git read-tree $OLD; git add <your explicit paths>
  git diff --cached --name-status $OLD      # confirm ONLY your paths
  TREE=$(git write-tree)
  NEW=$(printf '%s\n' "msg..." | git commit-tree $TREE -p $OLD)
  git update-ref refs/heads/main $NEW $OLD  # compare-and-swap: fails if HEAD moved
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat                # and READ IT
update-ref with the OLD sha is a genuine compare-and-swap, so it is safe against the race I-1222 describes AND does not touch index.lock. Landed my row as 671e4c657a this way after two plain-commit timeouts.

I did NOT delete the lock file: other lanes are live and I-1504 warns against removing it blind. The plumbing route makes deleting it unnecessary.

1	# LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
2	
3	LeanAG Horizon is a multi-project Lean 4 and Mathlib workspace for formalizing algebraic
4	geometry with [Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon). Its central goal is
5	the algebraic-geometry version of the [Algebraic Jacobian challenge](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian.20challenge/near/587802685),
6	proposed by Christian Merten after Kevin Buzzard's differential-geometry challenge.
7	
8	> [!IMPORTANT]
9	> The workspace develops **two live routes** to the Algebraic Jacobian challenge. Follow the
10	> project named by the active task rather than treating either route as reference-only.
11	>
12	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` continues the ambitious Picard-scheme route, building
13	>   representability by the Milne–Kollár construction of `Pic^r`, then `Pic^0` and the Albanese
14	>   property. Its Grassmannian, graded-algebra and flattening-stratification substrate is sorry-free
15	>   and still consumed, but the Quot-scheme endgame it was first written for is not the path being
16	>   built. Since 2026-07-28 its headline is stated over an arbitrary base field, with
17	>   representability asked of the étale-sheafified Picard functor and no rational-point hypothesis.
18	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` develops a cleaner curve-specialized route
19	>   from protected target statements.
20	
21	The two projects share mathematical sources and supporting subprojects while keeping independent
22	Lean roots, blueprints, and roadmaps. The rebuild is listed first in the workspace manifest as the
23	default project; explicitly scoped tasks may and do advance the ambitious original route.
24	
25	The [live dashboard](https://axeldlv00.github.io/LeanAlgebraicGeometry/) is the best view of current
26	tasks, commits, session logs, blueprint graphs, and declaration-level progress. A static snapshot
27	is published approximately every 30 minutes; GitHub Pages deployment and caching can add a few
28	minutes before a new snapshot is visible.

64	## Working in a Main Project
65	
66	The workspace currently uses Lean and Mathlib `v4.31.0`. Build the project named by the task. For
67	the ambitious Picard-scheme route:

70	cd MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge

76

80	horizon dashboard
81	horizon graph -p Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge frontier
82	horizon search "Jacobian Picard representability"
83	```

86	for the active project, and search queries declarations across the workspace and Mathlib.
87

90	landed work (archived inbox item `I-0501`). The scanner also invents declarations from docstring
91	prose, and some arrive marked `sorry`, so the frontier can list nodes that do not exist (archived
92	`I-0472`). Both defects were reproduced and neither was fixed.

94	## Methodology
95	
96	[Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon) coordinates long-running
97	formalization while keeping mathematical and operational state explicit:
98	
99	- **Horizon sessions** implement and verify Lean proofs against concrete tasks.
100	- **Fresh-context reviewers** such as Ground, work-reviewer, and janitor are dispatched at review
101	  and maintenance checkpoints rather than acting as a permanent second driver.
102	- **Blueprint graphs (`hgraph`)** track declaration dependencies, proof status, comments, and the
103	  ranked frontier for each project.
104	- **Roadmap, tasks, and inbox** record strategy, scoped work, cross-session handoffs, and durable
105	  failure memory.
106	- **The workspace ledger** records coherent commits and powers the public dashboard's progress
107	  and session views.
108	
109	Concurrent sessions can share a project's root import file. When adding one
110	import, build the staged root from the ledger's current `HEAD` and insert only
111	that line; do not stage the whole on-disk root, which may contain another
112	session's uncommitted imports.
113	
114	The mathematical blueprint is kept separate from implementation journals. Lean-specific progress
115	and failed approaches belong in graph comments, tasks, or the inbox, while the blueprint remains a
116	timeless account of the mathematics.
117

name: horizon-inbox
description: Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create; per-team ownership and read-state; and message other projects or teams via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
---

The inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and
future), and other projects. Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files
by hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or
fields.

## Read

- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,
  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters
  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,
  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,
  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.
- In an agent session, an unqualified list means the **open working queue**, not
  archived history. It is ordered by attention: required protections first,
  unread/direct conversations next, then advisory items. JSON starts with an
  `attention` summary so redirecting stderr cannot erase this signal.
- `horizon inbox show <id> --json` opens exactly one item and marks it read for
  your team. Use `--no-mark-read` for inspection without acknowledgement.
- Every inbox command evaluates the full local working set, even when `list` is
  filtered. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale
  memories, and consumed notices. The CLI never archives automatically because
  only the working agent can decide what is resolved; that agent must make an
  explicit cleanup pass before its final report.
- Labels are the release gate. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which
  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for
  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:
  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids
  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is
  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.
- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,
  `project:<name>`, or a **direct message** to another team: `task:<id>` /
  `run:<id>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience). A conversation
  may have several recipients; start one with `horizon inbox dm <recipient>...`.
  Scope/project says what the item is about.
- Horizon reads general items, items addressed to `horizon`, items addressed
  to its project, and DMs addressed to its own task/run. It should ignore other
  projects' and other teams' addressed items.
- A conversation's participants are its recipients **and its initiator**. The
  initiator is recorded as `metadata.started_by`; replies become unread for every
  other participant, including that initiator. Participants are not ownership:
  the initiator remains responsible for deciding when the thread is finished.
- Kinds: `conversation` (a direct/group thread requiring prompt acknowledgement),
  `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),
  `protection` (standing constraint / soft freeze), `info` (a notice for the
  human — something you did or noticed they should know, e.g. a renamed project
  or an important change; purely informational, never affects what runs),
  `memory` (durable agent note or dead end).

## Ownership & read-state (your team's inbox)

Each running session is a **team**, and the inbox is shared across teams. Two
lightweight overlays keep it navigable:

- **Ownership** — an item is either *shared with everyone* (the default) or
  *owned by one task* (that team's private inbox — e.g. its own memory). Read your
  team's inbox with `horizon inbox list --mine` (owned-by-you **plus** shared);
  another team's private items don't appear. Own an item to your task with
  `horizon inbox add --mine …` (or `--owner <task-id>`), and `horizon inbox own
  <id> --mine|--owner <task>|--shared` to move an existing one. Owning your
  `--kind memory` notes keeps another team's memory out of your working set.
- **Read-state** — read/unread is **per team**, so a shared item several teams see
  tracks who has read it. `horizon inbox list --unread` is what *you* have not read
  yet; `horizon inbox read <id>` marks it read, and `horizon inbox unread <id>`
  puts it back (e.g. you read it but it still needs action). Combine:
  `horizon inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue — the same signal
  the pre-command synchronizer counts for you.

1. `horizon inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json` — every
